verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西、亚伦说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron:

verses.zh: 「你们晓谕以色列人说：人若身患漏症，他因这漏症就不洁净了。
verses.en: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them, ‘When any man[NOTE:1] has a discharge[NOTE:2] from his body,[NOTE:3] his discharge is unclean.
notes: Heb “Man man.” The duplication is a way of saying “any man” (cf. Lev 17:3; 22:18, etc.; see the distributive repetition of the noun in GKC 395-96 §123.c).

The term “discharge” actually means “to flow,” whether referring to a full flow as at a spring of water (Ps 78:20 and parallels) or in reference to the promised land as “a land flowing with milk and honey” (Exod 3:8 and parallels).

Heb “when there is a discharge from his flesh.” It is well-recognized that the term “flesh” (i.e., “body”) in this chapter refers regularly and euphemistically to the male and female genital members or areas of the body (HALOT 164 s.v. בָּשָׂר 5.b; see also, e.g., B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 93). The euphemism has been retained in this translation since it is intended in the Hebrew text. Some English versions partially remove the euphemism (e.g., NAB “from his private parts”; NRSV “from his member”) while some remove it completely (e.g., NLT “a genital discharge”; TEV “from his penis”; CEV “with an infected penis”).

verses.zh: 他患漏症，无论是下流的，是止住的，都是不洁净。
verses.en: Now this is his uncleanness in regard to his discharge[NOTE:1]—whether his body secretes his discharge or blocks his discharge, he is unclean. All the days that his body has a discharge or his body blocks his discharge,[NOTE:2] this is his uncleanness.[NOTE:3]
notes: The LXX has “this the law of his uncleanness…” (cf. v. 32 and compare, e.g., 13:59; 14:2, 56).

The contrast between the dripping or flowing from the male sexual member as opposed to there being a blockage is important. One might not understand that even though a blockage actually causes a lack of discharge, it is still unclean.tc Smr, LXX, and the Paleo-Hebrew Leviticus Scroll from Qumran (11QpaleoLev; Fragment G contains Lev 14:52-15:5 and 16:2-4, and agrees with the LXX of Lev 15:3b) are in essential (although not complete) agreement against the MT in Lev 15:3b and are to be preferred in this case. The shorter MT text has probably arisen due to a lengthy haplography. See K. A. Mathews, “The Leviticus Scroll (11QpaleoLev) and the Text of the Hebrew Bible,” CBQ 48 (1986): 177-78, 198; D. N. Freedman, “Variant Readings in the Leviticus Scroll from Qumran Cave 11, ” CBQ 36 (1974): 528-29; D. N. Freedman and K. A. Mathews, The Paleo-Hebrew Leviticus Scroll, 32. The MT of Lev 15:3 reads: “Now this is his uncleanness in [regard to] his discharge—whether his body secretes his discharge or blocks his discharge, this is his uncleanness.” Smr adds after MT’s “blocks his discharge” the following: “he is unclean; all the days that his body has a discharge or his body blocks his discharge, this is his uncleanness.” Thus, the MT appears to skip from Smr הוא טמא “he is unclean” in the middle of the verse to טמאתו/הו יא “this is his uncleanness” at the end of the verse, leaving out “he is unclean; all the days that his body has a discharge or his body blocks his discharge” (cf. the BHS footnote). 11Q1 (paleoLeva frag. G) is indeed fragmentary, but it does have ימי ז בו כל “…in him, all the days of the fl[ow],” supporting Smr and LXX tradition. The LXX adds after MT “blocks his discharge” the following: “all the days of the flow of his body, by which his body is affected by the flow,” followed by “it is his uncleanness” (i.e., the last two words of the MT).

Heb “it is his uncleanness.” The last clause resumes the point of the first clause in this verse, while the material in between acts as parenthetic clarification. This verse introduces the regulations that follow in vv. 4ff.

verses.zh: 他所躺的床都为不洁净，所坐的物也为不洁净。
verses.en: “‘Any bed the man with a discharge lies on will be unclean,[NOTE:1] and any furniture he sits on will be unclean.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “All the bed which the man with a discharge sits on it shall be unclean”; cf. NLT “Any bedding.”
Heb “and all the vessel which he sits on it shall be unclean”; NASB “everything on which he sits.”

verses.zh: 凡摸那床的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。
verses.en: Anyone who touches his bed[NOTE:1] must wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And a man who touches in his bed”; NLT “touch the man’s bedding.”
Heb “he shall wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until the evening” (cf. also vv. 6-8, 10-11, etc.).

verses.zh: 那坐患漏症人所坐之物的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。
verses.en: The one who sits on the furniture the man with a discharge sits on must wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

verses.zh: 那摸患漏症人身体的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。
verses.en: The one who touches the body[NOTE:1] of the man with a discharge must wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
notes: Heb “And the one who touches in the flesh.” In this instance, “flesh” (or “body”) probably refers literally to any part of the body, not the genitals specifically (see the discussion in J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:914).

verses.zh: 若患漏症人吐在洁净的人身上，那人必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。
verses.en: If the man with a discharge spits on a person who is ceremonially clean,[NOTE:1] that person must wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
notes: Heb “And if the man with a discharge spits in the clean one.”

verses.zh: 患漏症人所骑的鞍子也为不洁净。
verses.en: Any means of riding[NOTE:1] that the man with a discharge rides on will be unclean.
notes: The Hebrew term for “means of riding” is a cognate noun from the verb “ride” later in this verse. It refers to anything on which one may ride without the feet touching the ground including, for example, a saddle, a (saddle) blanket, or a seat on a chariot (see, e.g., J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:916).

verses.zh: 凡摸了他身下之物的，必不洁净到晚上；拿了那物的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。
verses.en: Anyone who touches anything that was under him[NOTE:1] will be unclean until evening, and the one who carries those items[NOTE:2] must wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
notes: Heb “which shall be under him.” The verb is perhaps a future perfect, “which shall have been.”
Heb “them”; the referent (the previously mentioned items which were under the unclean person) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 患漏症的人没有用水涮手，无论摸了谁，谁必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。
verses.en: Anyone whom the man with the discharge touches without having rinsed his hands in water[NOTE:1] must wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
notes: Heb “And all who the man with the discharge touches in him and his hands he has not rinsed in water.”

verses.zh: 患漏症人所摸的瓦器就必打破；所摸的一切木器也必用水涮洗。
verses.en: A clay vessel[NOTE:1] which the man with the discharge touches must be broken, and any wooden utensil must be rinsed in water.
notes: The Hebrew term כְּלִי (keli) can mean “vessel” (v. 12a) or “utensil, implement, article” (v. 12b). An article of clay would refer to a vessel or container of some sort, while one made of wood would refer to some kind of tool or instrument.

verses.zh: 「患漏症的人痊愈了，就要为洁净自己计算七天，也必洗衣服，用活水洗身，就洁净了。
verses.en: “‘When the man with the discharge becomes clean from his discharge, he is to count off for himself seven days for his purification, and he must wash his clothes, bathe in fresh water,[NOTE:1] and be clean.
notes: For the expression “fresh water” see the note on Lev 14:5 above.

verses.zh: 第八天，要取两只斑鸠或是两只雏鸽，来到会幕门口、耶和华面前，把鸟交给祭司。
verses.en: Then on the eighth day he is to take for himself two turtledoves or two young pigeons,[NOTE:1] and he is to present himself[NOTE:2] before the Lord at the entrance of the Meeting Tent and give them to the priest,
notes: Heb “from the sons of the pigeon,” referring either to “young pigeons” or “various species of pigeon” (contrast J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:168 with J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 14; cf. Lev 1:14 and esp. 5:7-10).

The MT has the Qal form of the verb בּוֹא (boʾ) “to come” here, but the LXX (followed generally by the Syriac and Tg. Ps.-J.) reflects the Hiphil form of the same verb, “to bring” as in v. 29 below. In v. 29, however, there is no additional clause “and give them to the priest,” so the Hiphil is necessary in that context while it is not necessary here in v. 14.

verses.zh: 祭司要献上一只为赎罪祭，一只为燔祭；因那人患的漏症，祭司要在耶和华面前为他赎罪。
verses.en: and the priest is to make one of them a sin offering[NOTE:1] and the other a burnt offering.[NOTE:2] So the priest[NOTE:3] is to make atonement for him before the Lord for[NOTE:4] his discharge.
notes: See the note on Lev 4:3 regarding the term “sin offering.”
Heb “and the priest shall make them one a sin offering and the one a burnt offering.” See the note on Lev 1:3 regarding the “burnt offering.”
Heb “And the priest.” The Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) can be considered to have resultative force here.
Heb “from”; see the note on 4:26.

verses.zh: 「人若梦遗，他必不洁净到晚上，并要用水洗全身。
verses.en: “‘When a man has a seminal emission,[NOTE:1] he must bathe his whole body in water[NOTE:2] and be unclean until evening,
notes: Heb “And a man when a lying of seed goes out from him”; KJV, ASV “any man’s seed of copulation”; NIV, NRSV, TEV, NLT “an emission of semen.”
Heb “and he shall bathe all his flesh in water.”

verses.zh: 无论是衣服是皮子，被精所染，必不洁净到晚上，并要用水洗。
verses.en: and he must wash in water any clothing or leather that has semen on it, and it will be unclean until evening.

verses.zh: 若男女交合，两个人必不洁净到晚上，并要用水洗澡。
verses.en: As for a woman whom a man goes to bed with, then has a seminal emission,[NOTE:1] they must bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
notes: Heb “And a woman whom a man lies down with her, a lying of seed.” The verb שָׁכַב (shakhav) “to lie down” can imply going to bed for sexual relations. The phrase “a lying down of seed” or “an emission of seed” is adverbial, specifying the circumstance with which the regulation is concerned.

verses.zh: 「女人行经，必污秽七天；凡摸她的，必不洁净到晚上。
verses.en: “‘When a woman has a discharge[NOTE:1] and her discharge is blood from her body,[NOTE:2] she is to be in her menstruation[NOTE:3] seven days, and anyone who touches her will be unclean until evening.
notes: See the note on Lev 15:2 above.
Heb “blood shall be her discharge in her flesh.” The term “flesh” here refers euphemistically to the female sexual area (cf. the note on v. 2 above).
See the note on Lev 12:2 and R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 1:925-27.

verses.zh: 女人在污秽之中，凡她所躺的物件都为不洁净，所坐的物件也都不洁净。
verses.en: Anything she lies on during her menstruation will be unclean, and anything she sits on will be unclean.

verses.zh: 凡摸她床的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。
verses.en: Anyone who touches her bed must wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

verses.zh: 凡摸她所坐甚么物件的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。
verses.en: Anyone who touches any furniture she sits on must wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.

verses.zh: 在女人的床上，或在她坐的物上，若有别的物件，人一摸了，必不洁净到晚上。
verses.en: If there is something on the bed or on the furniture she sits on,[NOTE:1] when he touches it,[NOTE:2] he will be unclean until evening,
notes: Heb “and if on the bed it (הוּא, huʾ) is or on the vessel which she sits on it, when he touches it….” The translation and meaning of this verse is a subject of much debate in the commentaries (see the summary in J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:938-40). It is difficult to determine what הוּא refers to, whether it means “he” referring to the one who does the touching, “it” for the furniture or the seat in v. 22, “she” referring to the woman herself (see Smr היא rather than הוא), or perhaps anything that was lying on the furniture or the bed of vv. 21-22. The latter view is taken here (cf. J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 202).
The MT accent suggests that “when he touches it” goes with the preceding line, but it seems to be better to take it as an introduction to what follows (see J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 202).

verses.zh: 男人若与那女人同房，染了她的污秽，就要七天不洁净；所躺的床也为不洁净。
verses.en: and if a man actually goes to bed[NOTE:1] with her so that her menstrual impurity touches him,[NOTE:2] then he will be unclean seven days, and any bed he lies on will be unclean.
notes: Heb “actually lies down with.” The verb שָׁכַב (shakhav) “to lie down” acts as a euphemism, implying going to bed for sexual relations.
Heb “and if a man indeed lies with her and her menstrual impurity is on him.”

verses.zh: 「女人若在经期以外患多日的血漏，或是经期过长，有了漏症，她就因这漏症不洁净，与她在经期不洁净一样。
verses.en: “‘When a woman’s discharge of blood flows[NOTE:1] many days not at the time of her menstruation, or if it flows beyond the time of her menstruation,[NOTE:2] all the days of her discharge of impurity will be like the days of her menstruation—she is unclean.
notes: Heb “And a woman when the flow of her blood flows.”
Heb “in not the time of her menstruation or when it flows on her menstruation.”

verses.zh: 她在患漏症的日子所躺的床、所坐的物都要看为不洁净，与她月经的时候一样。
verses.en: Any bed she lies on all the days of her discharge will be to her like the bed of her menstruation, any furniture she sits on will be unclean like the impurity of her menstruation,

verses.zh: 凡摸这些物件的，就为不洁净，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。
verses.en: and anyone who touches them will be unclean, and he must wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.[NOTE:1]
notes: See the note on v. 5 above.

verses.zh: 女人的漏症若好了，就要计算七天，然后才为洁净。
verses.en: “‘If[NOTE:1] she becomes clean from her discharge, then she is to count off for herself seven days, and afterward she will be clean.
notes: Heb “And if….” Although this clause is parallel to v. 13 above, it begins with וְאִם (veʾim, “and if”) here rather than וְכִי (vekhi, “and when/if”) there.

verses.zh: 第八天，要取两只斑鸠或是两只雏鸽，带到会幕门口给祭司。
verses.en: Then on the eighth day she must take for herself two turtledoves or two young pigeons,[NOTE:1] and she must bring them to the priest at the entrance of the Meeting Tent,
notes: Heb “from the sons of the pigeon,” referring either to “young pigeons” or “various species of pigeon” (contrast J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:168 with J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 14; cf. Lev 1:14 and esp. 5:7-10).

verses.zh: 祭司要献一只为赎罪祭，一只为燔祭；因那人血漏不洁，祭司要在耶和华面前为她赎罪。
verses.en: and the priest is to make one a sin offering and the other a burnt offering.[NOTE:1] So the priest[NOTE:2] is to make atonement for her before the Lord from her discharge of impurity.
notes: Heb “And the priest shall make the one a sin offering and the one a burnt offering.”
Heb “And the priest.” The Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) can be considered to have resultative force here.

verses.zh: 「你们要这样使以色列人与他们的污秽隔绝，免得他们玷污我的帐幕，就因自己的污秽死亡。」
verses.en: “‘Thus you[NOTE:1] are to set the Israelites apart from their impurity so that they[NOTE:2] do not die in their impurity by defiling my tabernacle which is in their midst.
notes: Heb “And you shall.” The Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) can be considered to have resultative force here (cf. KJV, ASV, NASB, NCV, NRSV).
Heb “and they.” Here the Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) indicates a negative purpose (“lest,” so NAB, NASB).

verses.zh: 这是患漏症和梦遗而不洁净的，
verses.en: This is the law for the one with a discharge: for the one who has a seminal emission[NOTE:1] and becomes unclean by it,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and who a lying down of seed goes out from him.”
Heb “to become unclean in it.”

verses.zh: 并有月经病的和患漏症的，无论男女，并人与不洁净女人同房的条例。
verses.en: for the one who is sick in her menstruation, for the one with a discharge, whether male or female,[NOTE:1] and for a man who goes to bed[NOTE:2] with an unclean woman.’”
notes: Heb “and the one with a discharge, his discharge to the male and the female.”
Heb “who lies down with.” The verb שָׁכַב (shakhav) “to lie down” acts as a euphemism, implying going to bed for sexual relations.
